title: vendor lock graph and distro policy hook for isolated installs
author: Monica Li
release_notes: Adds a deterministic vendor-lock graph generator, kube-distro policy hooks for distro-specific overlay selection, and a small backward-compatible CLI flag for airgap bundle generation. Improves bundle size stability and preflight validation for on-prem installs.
description: Motivation: customers with strict air-gapped installs ran into nondeterministic vendor bundles when we deduplicated images and packages across distro overlays. This caused cache misses during local registry seeding and made atomic promotes brittle. This PR implements a vendor-lock graph generator (content-addressed), plus a distro policy hook that selects the minimal overlay set per target distro and kernel variant. The generator emits a stable lockfile and a compact delta manifest used by the offline bundler and the terraform seeder. Changes are backward-compatible: existing bundle formats are supported and the new CLI toggles are opt-in. What changed: 1) build/airgap/vendor-graph: new generator that computes content-addressed artifact nodes, canonicalizes package order, and produces a vendor-lock.json with checksums; 2) installer/preflight: verify vendor-lock checksums, support quick-fail when local registry lacks promoted layers; 3) charts/overlays/distro-selectors: small policy DSL (YAML) + selector runtime used by the bundler to pick only necessary overlays for k3s/rke2/kubeadm; 4) terraform/registry-seed: hook to ingest vendor-lock and apply atomic promote semantics to multi-repo mirrors; 5) docs and examples: updated airgap quickstart and migration notes. Testing: unit tests for graph canonicalization, e2e on small k3s image set using local registry mirror, manual validation of delta promotion on a seeded mirror. Backwards compat: when the flags are not set the bundler falls back to previous behavior. Rollout: feature gated by CLI --vendor-lock and controlled in Private Console for initial customers. Migration notes: existing customers should regenerate bundles to benefit from dedupe and smaller deltas. See linked linear tasks for rollout plan and telemetry collection.
